Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

1. Scope ' Dimensional and other requirements of tuber band for orthopaedic calipers and braces. 

2. Terminology 

2,1 Tuber B'*nd — Also known as ischeal band or seat should precisely fit just below the ischeal 
tuberosity to support the body weight. 



3. Shape and Dimensions As shown in Fkj 1 .

FIG 1 TUBER BAND FOR ORFHOPAEDIC CALIPERS AND BRACES 



4. Material — Mild steel sheet, cold-rolled; or aluminium. 

5. Workmanship and Finish — The band shall be cut to size as shown in Fig. 1. It shall be 
reasonably flat and the surfaces shall be free from defects. The cut edges shall bo rounded by 
grinding or filing. The final bending, tilting and flattening of seat of the band shall be done to suit 
the requirements of the individual at the lime of fitting the brace. 



Adopted 28 August 1980 



(O October 1980, BIS 



Gri 



BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS 
MANAK BHAVAN 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARG 



18:6224-1980 

6. Marking — Each band shall be marked with the following: 

a ) Manufacturer's name, initials or recognized trade-mark; and 
b ) Size of the band. 

6.1 Certification Marking - Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

7. Packing — As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard has been revised keeping in view the development and the experience gained by 
the industry. It also incorporates one additional extra large size. 



Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India
